title: "Projects & Methods"

This page is intentionally broader than a publication list. It highlights the problems, mathematical tools and computational methods that I use across projects.

## Holographic Krylov reconstruction

**Problem.** Reconstruct Krylov spread complexity from thermal partition functions and understand whether its growth admits a geometric bulk representation.

**Methods.** Lanczos recursion, spectral measures, orthogonal polynomials, high-order series, asymptotic fitting, analytical resummation, maximal-volume slices, extrinsic-curvature invariants.

**Tools.** Wolfram Mathematica, symbolic manipulation, numerical root finding, asymptotic analysis and data fitting.

## Charged black-hole information constraints

**Problem.** Use information-theoretic monotonicity to constrain allowed black-hole merger processes in charged AdS gravity.

**Methods.** Rényi entropies, black-hole thermodynamics, phase structure, extremality analysis, analytical approximations and numerical parameter scans.

## Spectral reconstruction of Krylov dynamics

**Problem.** Infer recurrence coefficients and continuum Krylov dynamics directly from partition-function or spectral data.

**Methods.** Edgeworth expansions, large deviations, orthogonal polynomials, spectral edges, continuum asymptotics and recurrence-coefficient analysis.

## Krylov complexity and stochastic systems

**Problem.** Explore whether recurrence structures in solvable stochastic models can classify universality regimes of Krylov transport.

**Methods.** ASEP, Askey–Wilson structures, edge universality, JT/KPZ-inspired scaling limits and integrable-model techniques.

## Technical toolkit

- **Wolfram Mathematica:** symbolic algebra, asymptotic series, numerical solvers, recurrence relations, high-order coefficient generation and resummation workflows.
- **Python:** scientific computing and numerical analysis; currently expanding toward broader research and quantitative workflows.
- **Mathematical methods:** spectral analysis, perturbation theory, orthogonal polynomials, random-matrix methods, asymptotics and statistical physics.
- **Scientific communication:** research talks, posters, teaching and collaborative writing in international teams.
